locator.section: 8.3 Steric factors -- hydrogen rearrangements in saturated OE+. ions

evidence.curator_note: EXPERIMENTAL CONTEXT: molecular ion (OE+., n-ionized at oxygen) of trans-4-tert-butylcyclohexanol undergoing water loss (Green et al. 1970); the page gives no electron energy, so ms_context.electron_energy_ev is null (not assumed 70 eV). This is the FAVORED (upper) branch of eq 8.26. The book states the tertiary H on the ring carbon bearing the tert-butyl group is transferred onto the -OH+. hydroxyl through a six-membered transition state, accessible only after a chair-to-boat conformational excitation (~0.5 eV); that pre-equilibrium is drawn as a double-headed equilibrium arrow (no bond change) and is NOT encoded as a step. The odd electron on the O+. radical cation abstracts the tertiary C4-H, forming the -OH2+ oxonium and leaving a tertiary radical on C4 (distonic radical cation, drawn explicitly on the page as the middle-right structure with a dot on the ring). Book draws 2 arc(s) on the boat structure; moves <1,2> are drawn (a large sweeping arc from the O+. odd electron to the transferring H forming the O-H bond, and a small fishhook routing one C4-H bonding electron into the same forming O-H bond), move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (the other C4-H bonding electron staying on C4 as the new radical, shown only by the dot drawn on the product ring, not as an arc). SIX-MEMBERED TS ring = O7-C1-C2-C3-C4-H12. STEREOCHEMISTRY NOT ENCODED: the mapped_smiles is the flat (achiral) connectivity; cis/trans differ only in the relative configuration of the OH and tert-butyl groups (not captured here). The whole point of eq 8.26 is that this relative stereochemistry makes the six-membered H-transfer TS geometrically accessible in the trans isomer (this record) but not in the cis isomer (see IMS8-EQ8.26b).

locator.section: 8.3 Steric factors -- hydrogen rearrangements in saturated OE+. ions

evidence.curator_note: Second step (labelled 'i' on the reaction arrow = inductive cleavage). The distonic -OH2+ oxonium loses water: the C1-O sigma bond cleaves heterolytically with BOTH electrons going onto the oxygen (which departs as neutral H2O), migrating the charge to C1 as a secondary carbocation. Because the tertiary radical stays on C4, the product is the (M - H2O)+. radical cation, a 1,4-distonic ion here (its subsequent ring closure / rearrangement to the observed alkene radical cation is not drawn). Book draws 1 arc: a single double-barbed (2-electron) arrow from the C1-O bond onto the oxygen; move <1> matches it exactly. (The +2 non-bonding electrons arriving on O are a lone pair, not two radicals -- reported by the arrow checker as a soft lone-pair note.)

No MOD rule corresponds to equation 8.26. rule_index.json by_equation covers chapter 8 only up to '8.14'; there is no by_equation['8.26'] entry, so there is nothing to cross-link and no rule_mismatch to report for this scheme.

observed_mz 138.1403 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of the (M - H2O)+. radical cation C10H18+. (electron-mass corrected). The page prints the product only symbolically as '(M - H2O)+.' with NO numeric m/z and NO intensity, so status is 'inferred', detected=false, and relative_intensity is omitted. Water loss from the trans isomer is the experimentally favored process discussed in the text, but no percentage is given on this page.
